title: Why are we ruled by barbarians?
gist: Noah Smith argues that America's New Right, defined by a civilizational 'Western' identity, a Europe obsession and a cult of toughness, embraces savagery as political style, as shown by the proposed televised firing-squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan and pro-Russia tilt. He says this is a fringe worldview unpopular with most Americans but likely to outlast Trump.

insights.claim: The Trump administration planned a televised firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, then cancelled the livestream after polling showed nearly every segment of American society opposed it except MAGA Republican men.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Shows the gap between the New Right's preferences and the median voter, which constrains what it can pursue politically.

insights.claim: Smith argues the episode reveals that the men now ruling America hold premodern, barbaric values unlike the average American's.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Political risk from governance driven by a fringe worldview rather than broad consensus.
insights.quote: They are, in many ways, premodern and barbaric.

insights.claim: Trump leads the New Right but is old, visibly declining and not fundamentally of it, so the New Right ideology rather than another charismatic figure will fill the vacuum, possibly in a purer form without Trump's corruption baggage.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Plan for post-Trump continuity of the ideology, not a reversion to establishment conservatism.
insights.locator: It is very important that we understand the New Right

insights.claim: The New Right rules through factional politics, in which a small minority becomes the majority-of-a-majority-of-a-majority.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Narrow factional coalitions can win power without broad support, raising policy volatility.
insights.locator: It is very important that we understand the New Right

insights.claim: The New Right defines Western Civilization by European descent, Christian heritage and veneration of both, including Russia but excluding Japan and Latin America, with Christianity as heritage and boundary more than faith.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: This civilizational lens explains foreign-policy alignments that look odd under a Cold War 'free world' frame.
insights.quote: It’s less about Christ than about Christendom.
insights.locator: The New Right, Western Civilization, and the Europe obsession

insights.claim: The New Right cares about Europe more than any prior American right, whereas the Old Old Right of 1910 to 1935 was isolationist and hostile to South and East European immigrants, as in the 1924 immigration law.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Transatlantic ties now depend on ideological affinity with Europe's right rather than traditional alliance logic.
insights.locator: The New Right, Western Civilization, and the Europe obsession

insights.claim: Rubio, Hegseth and Vance have all framed mass migration, especially from Muslim countries, as an invasion destroying Western civilization, aided by European leftist elites.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Administration rhetoric ties US-Europe policy to migration politics.

insights.claim: Rioting in France is boosting the European right, with one commentator cited putting Le Pen's chances close to 1 in 2.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: French political risk is rising; watch the French election and European assets.

insights.claim: The US New Right views itself as allied or identical with the European right, with Musk backing AfD, Vance meeting AfD and campaigning for Orban, and Trump supporting Le Pen, though Trump's unpopularity in Europe often hurts those parties.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: US endorsements may be an electoral liability for European right parties.

insights.claim: Most Americans do not link European migration problems to US immigration; pro-immigrant attitudes have surged since Trump returned and the President is underwater on immigration, so the Europe-centered worldview is a fringe belief.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The movement's core beliefs lack mass appeal, limiting durable electoral support.
insights.locator: Regular Americans simply do not see Europe and America as a single entity

insights.claim: The New Right treats electoral failure as a result of being too meek, unlike leftists who blame insufficient ideological purity, and so prizes toughness and brutality, citing figures like Michael Anton, Jesse Kelly and Donald Trump Jr.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Expect escalation of tough-guy policy and rhetoric after setbacks rather than moderation.
insights.quote: Rightists, on the other hand, are obsessed with toughness.
insights.locator: A pattern should begin to emerge here

insights.claim: American rightists praise Franco and Pinochet as effective through savagery and increasingly invoke Hitler to signal ruthlessness.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Rhetorical radicalization is a marker of where the movement may move.

insights.claim: Part of the Trump-Russia romance is that the right sees Putin's Russia as living Western toughness, which Smith cites to explain cancelled Russia sanctions, urging Europe to buy Russian gas, cutting Starshield communications to Ukraine and joint economic projects.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Ideological affinity, not only corruption, drives pro-Russia policy, so it may persist beyond Trump.
insights.locator: the rightist obsession with toughness explains part of the romance

insights.claim: The MAGA ideology views Russia as a civilizational ally against an EU it believes captured by leftists and importing anti-Western immigrants.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Predicts continued US pressure on the EU and softness toward Moscow.
insights.locator: The MAGA ideology views Russia as a civilizational ally

insights.claim: The New Right's savagery also supports a fantasy of a ruthless vanguard of 'three percent' that would win a post-democratic civil war, compensating for unpopularity and losing the young generation of men.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The dangerous self-image raises tail risk of political violence and poor strategic choices.
insights.locator: The only way for rightists to sustain the illusion

insights.claim: A successful movement needs broad popular appeal, not just willingness to out-barbarize the enemy, so the New Right's chosen strategy is likely to produce mistakes.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Expect electoral backlash against the New Right's strategy.
insights.quote: A successful movement needs broad popular appeal, not just the willingness to out-barbarize the enemy.
